context.note: Queue task 325, GH#625, stage S5. TEST-DESIGNER's own acceptance test (test/letflow/engine/wasm/module_version_registry_test.exs, commit f8ec561, the core overlapping-activation scenario proving AC1/2/3/5) fails at its very first register_version/3 call: {:error, {:instantiation_failed, {:unresolved_import, "env", "platform_call_service"}}}. This is a REAL, load-bearing design defect, not a test-writing mistake. ORCH root-caused it directly: ModuleRegistry.register/1 (REQ-166, unmodified, correctly untouched per this design's own composition-over-modification approach) has an explicitly documented, deliberate scope (module_registry.ex's own moduledoc, quoting req163-wasm-abi-choice.md SS4): its stage-2 real-instantiation check calls Wasmex.start_link(%{bytes: bytes}) with NO imports map at all, and 'an instantiation failure -- including an unresolved import -- is rejected identically to a missing/malformed export: at registration, not first invocation.' This means ModuleRegistry.register/1 structurally CANNOT ever succeed for a module that imports ANY host function -- which is exactly what req173_v1_gated.wat/req173_v2_gated.wat (this design's own SS8 test fixtures, importing platform_call_service / write_variable) need to do to exercise real capability-gated invocations, the actual point of WASM-14's test. The design's SS3 register_version/3 spec (lines ~161-170) states 'Stage 1/2 ABI validation (ModuleRegistry.register/1) runs in the CALLING process' as its ENTIRE validation step -- it never accounts for capability-requiring modules at all. This is precisely the class of gap this project's design gate exists to catch, and it was missed in both design-validation rounds because neither traced whether the design's own chosen test fixtures could actually pass register_version/3's specified validation path. The already-shipped, gate-approved mechanism for capability-aware instantiation already exists: CapabilityGate.start_instance/2 (capability_gate.ex ~445-470) builds the manifest-derived import table via build_import_table/1 and attempts a real instantiation against it (returning {:error, {:instantiation_denied, instantiation_defect()}} on any disallowed/unresolved import), structurally identical in spirit to ModuleRegistry.register/1's stage-2 except capability-aware and NOT auto-stopping the instance (since it's meant to hand back a live instance to invoke, not a throwaway proof).

task.description: REWORK REQUIRED. Fix register_version/3's validation path so it can actually succeed for a module requiring host capabilities declared in its own manifest, without weakening ABI validation for modules that don't need any. Design options to weigh (pick one, justify it): (a) keep ModuleRegistry.register/1's stage-1 ABI/export check (Wasmex.Module.compile/2 + exports/1 -- these never instantiate, so they're capability-agnostic and fine as-is), but replace or supplement its stage-2 zero-import instantiation proof with a capability-aware proof using CapabilityGate.build_import_table/2 (the version's own manifest) + a bounded instantiation attempt (mirroring CapabilityGate.start_instance/2's own pattern -- Task.Supervisor.async_nolink under a task supervisor, Task.yield with a timeout, GenServer.stop on the proving instance since register_version/3 only needs a PROOF here, unlike start_instance/2's real-instance contract) -- i.e. register_version/3 does its OWN capability-aware instantiation proof rather than delegating that specific step to ModuleRegistry.register/1; (b) some other approach you can justify as correctly handling both a capability-requiring module and a capability-free module (e.g. building the import table from an empty-capabilities manifest fallback -- but justify why that's not equivalent to option (a) with a wasted step). Whichever you choose, be explicit about which of ModuleRegistry.register/1's two stages you still reuse verbatim vs. which you must reimplement or supplement, and update SS3/SS4/SS5 accordingly. Re-verify (live, against real source, not narrative) that your chosen mechanism will actually let req173_v1_gated.wat and req173_v2_gated.wat (or updated fixtures, if you choose to change them) register successfully. Also re-check whether this changes anything about SS6's crash-safety/ref-counting argument (a second Task.Supervisor.async_nolink call in register_version/3's own validation, if you add one, must not introduce a THIRD timeout-classification path beyond invoke/4's already-approved two). Do not otherwise touch the already-approved invoke/4 dispatch mechanism (SS3/SS4's timeout classification, checkout, ref counting, capability isolation) unless this fix genuinely requires it.
acceptance_criteria: a test holds an invocation open (a guest blocked in a controllable host call), activates a new module version DURING it, and asserts the held invocation completes normally against the OLD version's observable behaviour -- WASM-14's own acceptance criterion, with the overlap real rather than sequential
the same test asserts an invocation started AFTER the activation observes the NEW version's behaviour, so both halves of WASM-14 are proven in one overlapping scenario
the two module versions used are observably different in output, so the test can distinguish which version served an invocation rather than merely completing
a test asserts the prior version's resources are released only after its last in-flight invocation completes, not at activation time

a test asserts that when the new version's manifest declares a DIFFERENT capability set, an in-flight invocation of the prior version keeps the prior version's capability set, and the new invocation gets the new one -- so activation cannot silently widen or narrow a running invocation's authority
mix test and mix compile --warnings-as-errors both pass with real output quoted
a module requiring at least one host capability can be successfully registered via register_version/3 -- verified by an actual passing test, not merely a design claim
